test.name: Flag a spouse absent from the household even though the tree records her death decades later
test.description: Variant of ut_person_evidence_026 on the scenario census-household-spouse-died-later. The 1860 census household of George Ackerman (assertions a_001-a_007: head + children Henry and Margaret) is the same; the difference is that George's wife Catherine (I2, Couple R1) now carries a sourced Death fact dated 3 Mar 1884. A death 24 years after the record does not explain her absence from it, so she is still expected in the household and must still be flagged. Guards the household check against skipping anyone with any death fact: project_context's diedByYear is 1884, after the record's year, so Catherine is checked. ut_026 cannot catch that defect because its Catherine has no death fact.

input.delegation:
person-evidence: I've extracted George Ackerman's 1860 census household into research.json (assertions a_001-a_007). George is already in the tree (I1). Link these assertions to persons and build out this household skeleton in the tree.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The record's household is George Ackerman (head, a_001 -> already linked to I1 via pe_001) plus two children absent from the tree: Henry (child_1: name a_002, birth a_003) and Margaret (child_2: name a_005, birth a_006). Each child must be MINTED carrying its sourced census facts via materialize_facts create-or-enrich (name + birth with source-refs, and whatever gender the record supports: this census carries no sex assertion for either child, so materialize_facts writes Unknown and that is correct, not malformed, not a name-only shell) and linked, and the George->Henry / George->Margaret parent-child edges (relationship assertions a_004 / a_007, src_001 -> tree source S1) written via tree_edit add_relationship with a source-ref at LOWER ref quality (a pre-1880 census parent-child edge is INDIRECT). A merge_warnings dry-run is a plus, not required (pre-extracted assertions, no candidate document).

THE DIMENSION UNDER TEST: George's wife Catherine (I2) is in the tree, joined to George by the Couple relationship R1, and her Death fact is dated 3 Mar 1884, 24 years AFTER this 1860 census. Her death therefore does not explain her absence, so she would be expected in an 1860 household George heads. She does NOT appear among the record's personas (there is no assertion for her). The agent must, ON ITS OWN, surface Catherine's unexplained absence as an identity/research question. Pass requires the agent to flag this absence; treat the 'Person minting and connecting edges' dimension as the anchor for it.

What counts as the flag: a reply that names Catherine's absence from this household and offers possible explanations (she was enumerated elsewhere, was omitted, separated, or this is a different family) IS the required flag, wherever in the reply it appears; it need not use the words 'identity question'. Not mentioning her absence at all is a FAIL. Saying she is absent BECAUSE she had died, or skipping her because the tree records a death, is also a FAIL: her recorded death is in 1884, after the record. Naming death before 1860 as one possibility among others is acceptable only if the reply does not treat the 1884 death as settling it. A separate dismissal of a `person_warnings` date-plausibility warning (for example an age-at-death check) is not a dismissal of Catherine's absence and does not undo the flag.

DERIVATION, NOT ECHO: the absence is stated nowhere the agent is handed - not in the user message, not in the log_001 notes, not in any assertion or citation (all of which mention only the head and the two children). Crediting the flag requires the agent to have COMPARED George's tree family (which includes wife Catherine via R1) against the record roster and derived that she is missing.

The agent must NOT 'resolve' the absence by renaming or overwriting Catherine (I2) to match a record persona, nor fabricate an assertion or persona for her, nor edit or remove her Death fact. Flagging the open question is the complete, correct response; adjudicating why she is absent belongs to later research, not to this link step.

Tool Arguments: minting the children and writing the edges is the expected tool use. If the skill additionally reasons from the tree + assertions without an extra query, that is fine; no same_person call is required (the head is already linked and the children are new stubs, not identity matches).
